title: TCH → trastuzumab continuation

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
agents.watch: Take prescribed steroid premedication. Report fever, lasting numbness, swelling, sore nails or infusion symptoms.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Hair loss, mouth soreness and fatigue

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen.
agents.watch: Keep blood-test appointments. Fever, unusual bleeding, repeated vomiting or infusion symptoms need prompt advice.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Allergic reaction, sometimes after previous exposure

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments throughout HER2 treatment. Report breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or a reaction; chemotherapy side effects are tracked separately.

purpose: Treat HER2-positive early breast cancer as part of a plan intended to reduce the risk of it returning.
schedule_summary: Default: six 21-day TCH cycles with IV trastuzumab, then trastuzumab alone to complete one year total. The source also permits weekly IV or fixed-dose SC trastuzumab alternatives; the team confirms the formulation and visit schedule.

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: Relative sequence, not equal lengths or booked dates. Your team confirms actual appointments and the active medicines.
timeline_note: Treatment markers show the planned schedule. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves; serious symptoms can occur at any time.
safety_note: Fever, shivers, sudden illness, severe breathing changes or chest pain need prompt assessment on any day.
teachback: Which medicines are active now, which days do you receive or take them, and who is booking and reviewing your next tests?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, common and serious effects, fertility and pregnancy precautions, route, monitoring, practical support and the agreed contact plan. The treating team completes the approved individual consent process.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, jaundice, unusual bleeding or sudden illness promptly. Do not wait for the next planned test.

support.title: The correct supportive prescription
support.text: Follow the script for the active medicine, route and treatment day. Do not carry chemotherapy anti-sickness medicines automatically into an antibody-only phase.

support.title: Tests before treatment
support.text: NCCP specifies baseline and regular FBC, liver and renal profiles; the team confirms the pre-dose checks for the active chemotherapy or trastuzumab-only phase. Verify kidney function for carboplatin dosing.

support.title: Keep heart checks on the plan
support.text: An echo every 12 weeks is separate from blood tests or cancer imaging. Ask who books and reviews it.

support.title: Plan for symptoms
support.text: Keep your agreed contact numbers and instructions. New symptoms can need assessment before a routine appointment.

questions.a: Ask the team who books each test, who checks the result and who to contact if an appointment is overdue. This map does not book appointments.

questions.q: What if I become unwell between visits?
questions.a: Use the urgent contact plan for sudden illness, fever, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea or poor fluid intake. Do not wait for a scheduled blood test or scan.

TCH is an adjuvant treatment after surgery for HER2-positive early breast cancer. Docetaxel and carboplatin provide chemotherapy without an anthracycline, with trastuzumab targeting HER2. Recurrence risk, lymph nodes, heart and kidney function, fitness and alternative treatments affect selection. Trastuzumab continues after chemotherapy to complete the agreed course.

questions.q: When is my next heart scan?
questions.a: NCCP lists baseline echo/MUGA if clinically indicated, but requires cardiac eligibility assessment; the trastuzumab product information calls for baseline cardiac assessment. Repeat every 12 weeks during trastuzumab and at completion. Earlier checks follow symptoms or cardiac concern. Around cycle 5 is the first 12-week check if treatment stays on time.
Surgery comes before this adjuvant chemotherapy. Radiotherapy, if indicated, is coordinated after chemotherapy and may overlap trastuzumab or later endocrine treatment when agreed.

questions.q: Do I need regular scans or markers?
questions.a: Baseline breast and nodal imaging, with staging tests appropriate to the diagnosis. Review response during preoperative treatment and before surgery. After local treatment, arrange breast surveillance; routine CT, PET or tumour-marker testing is not the usual screening plan for someone without symptoms.

items.title: Bone health and endocrine treatment
items.text: If the cancer is also hormone-receptor positive, endocrine treatment may form part of the wider plan. Bone-density testing is linked to aromatase inhibitors, ovarian suppression and fracture risk; it is not automatically required because a HER2 medicine is prescribed. Agree baseline DEXA where indicated and individual follow-up.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Confirm blood tests, heart assessment, active medicines, route and the consent discussion.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit time and transport
details.text: First visits can take longer because of loading doses, premedicines and observation. Ask the unit about expected time, transport and any escort needed after sedation or line insertion.

details.title: Phase-specific visit pattern
details.text: Infusion and observation times differ by drug and first versus later doses; the unit confirms the full visit duration, including blood review and preparation.
